children: ASML Holding (ASML), the powerhouse behind advanced chipmaking lithography, rocketed 4.0% to $1,711.115 Friday. The catalyst was impossible to ignore: TSMC's
equipment requirements have climbed to approximately 1.9 times their year-end level as the chipmaker prepares to spend between $60 billion and $64 billion in 2026.

ASML is already turning that demand into serious numbers. Second-quarter revenue hit 9.33 billion, while net income reached 2.92 billion for a hefty 31.3% margin. Management expects full-year sales of 43 billion to 45 billion, putting the midpoint approximately 34.6% above 2025, and plans to lift low-NA EUV production capacity by roughly 30% for 2027.

Here is the catch: investors are no longer paying a bargain price for the growth. At $1,711.115, ASML trades 36.66% above its $1,250 GF Value estimate, signaling that the market already expects near-flawless execution. TSMC's spending boom strengthens the order outlook, but supplier bottlenecks, long installation cycles or customer-site delays could quickly test that premium.

title: ASML Rockets 4% as TSMC's Tool Hunger Nearly Doubles
